title: The RSI
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/0/body: The **RSI (Relative Strength Index)**, created by Welles Wilder, measures the strength of **recent gains versus recent losses** and moves between **0 and 100**. Its default period is **14**, and it's shown in a separate panel below the chart.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/1/body: **RS = average gain ÷ average loss** over the last 14 candles, and **RSI = 100 − 100 ÷ (1 + RS)**. The bigger the gains are compared with the losses, the closer RSI gets to 100.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/2/prompt: If the average gain and average loss over the last 14 candles are exactly equal, what's the RSI?
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/2/explan: When gains and losses are equal, RS = 1 and RSI = 100 − 100 ÷ 2 = 50. Neither side has the upper hand.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/3/statem: RSI can go above 100 or below zero.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/3/explan: The RSI formula always keeps it between 0 and 100. 100 means there were only gains, and 0 means only losses.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/4/prompt: RS (average gain ÷ average loss) is 3. What's the RSI?
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/5/body: RSI **above 50** means gains have outweighed losses recently (**bullish momentum**), and **below 50** means losses have dominated (**bearish momentum**). So the 50 line is the border between the two.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/5/tip: RSI is built only from closing prices. It's a second view of the same price, not new information.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/6/prompt: Look at the RSI panel. Which reading is right?
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/6/explan: RSI is hovering around 60 to 65. Gains are bigger than losses and momentum is bullish, but it hasn't reached overbought territory yet.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/7/senten: RSI moves between ___ and 100, and its default period is ___ candles.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/7/explan: The RSI range is always 0 to 100, and Wilder suggested a 14-period setting.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l1/steps/8/pairs/: Average gain divided by average loss
Border of bullish and bearish momentum
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/0/body: RSI **above 70** is called **overbought**, and **below 30** is called **oversold**: price has moved very fast in one direction. It's a **warning, not an order**. Price can stay in these zones for a while.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/1/title: A better signal: leaving the zone
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/1/body: Instead of selling the moment RSI hits 70, many traders wait for **RSI to drop back below 70** (or climb back above 30) and for **price to confirm**, like a reversal candle at a key level. This works best in a **ranging market**.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/2/prompt: Tap the candle where RSI went above 70.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/2/explan: After several bullish candles in a row, this candle pushed RSI past 70 and into overbought territory. The next candles brought RSI back below 70.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/3/prompt: Look at the RSI panel. What's the situation?
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/3/explan: After several bearish candles in a row, RSI has dropped below 30, so the selling was very fast. That alone isn't a reason to buy, but it says the move is stretched.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/4/statem: When RSI goes above 70, price has to drop right away.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/4/explan: Overbought only means the buying was fast. In strong trends, price can keep rising with RSI above 70.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/5/prompt: Price hit daily support after a sharp sell-off, RSI dropped below 30, and the last candle is a hammer. What's more likely?
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/5/explan: You have three clues pointing the same way: key support, an oversold RSI turning back up, and a hammer. A bounce is more likely, but not certain. Stop loss below the hammer's low.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/6/body: In volatile markets or strong trends, some traders change the levels to **80 and 20** to get **fewer but more reliable** signals. Wilder's standard setting is **70 and 30**.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/7/prompt: Why do some traders change the RSI levels to 80 and 20 in strong trends?
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/7/option: To get fewer but more reliable overbought/oversold signals
Because RSI goes above 100 in a trend
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/7/explan: In a strong trend, RSI hits 70 or 30 often, and false signals pile up. Stricter levels only flag the really stretched moves.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/8/prompt: EUR/USD is in a 1.0800 to 1.0860 range. Price has reached 1.0860, RSI has dropped from 74 to 68, and a shooting star closed at resistance. What's the most sensible move?
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/8/option: Sell with a stop above the high, target the middle or bottom of the range
Buy because RSI is still above 50
Sell without a stop because it's overbought
Buy with high leverage because it's an uptrend
lessons/oscillators-u1-l2/steps/8/explan: In a range, RSI dropping back below 70, plus resistance and a reversal candle, makes a sensible sell setup. But you always need a stop loss; the range could break.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/0/body: In a **strong uptrend**, RSI can stay **above 70** for a long time while price keeps rising. Selling just because it's "overbought" means standing in front of the trend.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/1/body: Many analysts have noticed that in an **uptrend**, RSI mostly swings between **40 and 80**, and pullbacks often end around **40 to 50**. In a **downtrend** it's the reverse: mostly between **20 and 60**, with rallies often stalling around **50 to 60**.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/1/tip: In an uptrend, see RSI pulling back to 40–50 as a buying chance. Don't wait for 30.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/2/prompt: Tap the candle where this uptrend's pullback ended (the pullback's lowest RSI).
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/2/explan: This candle is the low of the pullback, and RSI hit its lowest point (around 58) right here; it didn't even reach 50. The trend is very strong, and buyers came back fast.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/3/prompt: It's an uptrend. RSI pulled back from around 70 to near 50, and a strong bullish candle just closed. What's next?
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/3/explan: In an uptrend, RSI pulling back to the 40–50 zone and turning up usually means buyers are back. The trend is more likely to continue. Stop loss below the pullback low.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/4/statem: In a downtrend, RSI rallies often stall around 50 to 60.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/4/explan: In a downtrend, bearish momentum dominates, so RSI rallies usually give up below 60, and the 50–60 zone acts like resistance.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/5/prompt: The uptrend is strong, and RSI has stayed above 70 for 8 candles. Which move is a mistake?
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/5/option: Selling just because RSI is above 70
Waiting for a pullback and RSI near 40–50 to buy
Holding your earlier buy with a trailing stop
Checking levels and price structure before deciding
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/5/explan: Staying overbought is normal in a strong trend. Selling for that reason alone means trading against the trend. The other options are sensible moves.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/6/body: As long as RSI bounces back **above 40–50** on pullbacks, the uptrend is healthy. If RSI drops **below 40** and can't get past **50–60** on the next rally, the trend may be weakening or turning.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/7/prompt: Put the steps of a with-the-trend buy using RSI in order.
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/7/items/: Spot an uptrend (higher highs and lows)
RSI pulls back to the 40–50 zone
Enter with a stop below the pullback low
lessons/oscillators-u1-l3/steps/7/explan: RSI only improves your timing here. First the trend and price structure, then the pullback, then confirmation, and finally an entry with defined risk.
